editorial.tldr: Kimi K3.1 surfaced as an unreleased name after Arena testing, then Moonshot launched the roughly 3T-parameter K3.1 Pro on Oct 24. A quota-driven rocky rollout was followed by third-party hosting, vLLM day-0 support and, on Nov 5, full open weights.
editorial.whats_new: Moore Threads added day-zero Kimi K3.1 Pro support on its MTT S5000 GPUs on Nov 7, the second Chinese accelerator vendor after Huawei Ascend to support the open weights.
editorial.why_it_matters: K3.1 Pro is now self-hostable on vLLM, Ascend and MTT S5000, and vLLM's RL work shows it is also a fine-tuning target. Licence terms and a 1.56TB footprint decide whether that beats third-party hosts or first-party quotas.
editorial.take_for_builders: Read the weights licence conditions before planning a self-host, and budget for 1.56TB of storage. Pin the vLLM version and rerun your own evals against Opus 5.5 before changing routing; for RL, check the bit-for-bit kernel alignment in vLLM's post first.

status.detail: K3.1 Pro moved from a quota-troubled first-party launch to third-party hosting, vLLM support, full open weights and now a second Chinese accelerator (Moore Threads) beyond Huawei Ascend. Independent quality and cost data are still thin.
